# Leohang Illustrations — Article Illustration Skill

When asked to generate article illustrations, shot lists, or visual metaphors for Chinese content, follow these rules:

## Visual DNA
- 16:9 horizontal. Pure white background (no texture/gradient/shadow).
- Black hand-drawn line art, slightly wobbly pen lines. Lots of whitespace (subject 40-60%, at least 35% blank).
- Sparse Chinese handwritten annotations: max 5-8 spots, 2-8 chars each.
- One image = one core structure/metaphor.
- Colors: Black (main line art), Orange (flow/arrows), Red (warnings/results), Blue (supplementary notes). Restrained — less is more.

## Character: Leohang
Young man, short black hair, **rectangular black-framed glasses** (must be visible), black high-collar zip-up jacket, black trousers, white sneakers. Focused, calm, hands-on engineer. Must perform the core action, not decorate. If removing Leohang leaves the metaphor intact, he's too decorative — rewrite.

## Structure Types (pick one)
Workflow | System Partial | Before/After | Character State | Concept Metaphor | Method Layering | Map Route | Mini Comic Strip

## Metaphor Generation
1. Abstract concept → physical action (stuck, sorting, fermenting, weighing, opening)
2. System structure → low-tech object (broken machine, funnel, well, ladder, cardboard box)
3. Leohang bears the action — inside the machine, pulling wires, carrying, filtering

## Don'ts
No PPT, no cute cartoon, no formal flowchart, no gradients/shadows, no title in top-left, no mascot feel, no replicating known compositions.
